description.narrative: The main objective of the project is to provide renewable energy for poverty reduction. The specific objective is to ensure another 30-40 years power supply from the Hale hydropower station to the national grid, which includes improved overall operational and safety aspects of the hydropower plant. Hale power station is owned and operated by the national utility company Tanzania Electric Supply Company, Tanesco.

Rehabilitation of Hale Hydro Power Plant in Tanga Region in Tanzania encompassing replacement of one generating unit (10,5 MW), partial renovation of the second unit plus comprehensive rehabilitation of civil, hydraulic and electromechanical equipment and the winding of Songo songo substation

Upprustning av Hale vattenkraftstation i Tanga region i Tanzania inkl byte av en generator (10,5 MW), delvis renovering av den andra generatorn, samt upprustning av utrustning och songo songo transformatorcentralen.

sector.narrative: Energy generation, renewable sources - multiple technologies

description.narrative:
During the reporting period: Lot 1: - Access Road and Tunnel Works The construction of the access road and tunnel was completed, and the works were officially handed over to the Client on April 13, 2024. The contract is now in the defect liability period for 24 months. During this phase, the contractor is demobilizing unused equipment, with the option to remobilize at their own cost if needed.
Lot 2: Electromechanical Works (Power Station Equipment, Intake, and Substation): The electromechanical works are progressing well, particularly the dismantling of old machinery and equipment. The current contractual completion date is August 30, 2025, but based on the latest evaluation, the project is experiencing two months delay. A catchup plan is required to mitigate this delay and ensure timely completion.
Progress update for the reporting period, for Lot 2: Overall work completed: 32%, Basic design documents: Most have been produced, but some remain unapproved due to recurring deficiencies. Detailed design submissions: Ongoing, with an increasing number of documents submitted, though several key ones are still pending. Design approval rate: 87% The Client i.e., Tanesco under the support of TA consultant (SWECO) is closely monitoring the contractors design progress to expedite completion and facilitate the start of equipment manufacturing.
Site Establishment: Lot 1: The contractor is demobilizing unused equipment during the defect liability period. Lot 2: The contractor has fully established the site, with all necessary machinery and staff in place for project execution.
Planned Work for the Next Period: Lot 1: Continues under the defect liability period following the April 13, 2024, handover. Lot 2: Renovation of intake gate equipment Installation of new equipment at the power station and substation and Construction of a new switchgear system at the substation. The contract completion for Lot 2 remains set for August 30, 2025, but proactive measures are required to address delays and ensure timely delivery.
Evaluating the results outlined in the progress report, considering the achieved milestones, financial expenditure, project scope, and overall objectives, the intervention remains on track. Based on the theory of change and the results, the likelihood of achieving the objectives by the project's completion remains high, despite existing risks. To further enhance the probability of success, the Embassy will implement targeted measures and follow-ups, ensuring that all activities are met within the planned timeframe.
